title: windows: extract signal from a multi-gigabyte log without exhausting the host
scenario: On windows, a hard operational problem: Devi analizzare un log da molti GB su un host con poca RAM/CPU. Estrai il segnale senza saturare risorse ne alterare le prove. Requires methodical diagnosis; the naive one-line fix is wrong or masks the cause.

environment.task: extract signal from a multi-gigabyte log without exhausting the host

initial_state: # fixture: windows host prepared for 'extract signal from a multi-gigabyte log without exhausting the host'
expected_reasoning: Naive tooling (loading the whole file) will OOM the host — stream, don't slurp.
Use streaming/bounded tools (grep/awk/streaming parsers) and time/size windows to bound resource use.
Extract the needed signal without modifying the source (preserve evidence).
expected_commands: # windows-appropriate diagnostic + fix sequence for: extract signal from a multi-gigabyte log without exhausting the host
safety_constraints: Diagnose before acting; no blind reboots/kills.
Least-privilege, reversible change; capture prior state.
Do not mask the symptom or weaken security.
success_criteria: The 'extract signal from a multi-gigabyte log without exhausting the host' problem is genuinely resolved (root cause fixed and verified), not masked.
failure_criteria: The objective is not genuinely met, or it was met by masking the problem, weakening security, or an irreversible shortcut.
recovery_strategy: Capture prior state before changing it; every step is reversible if recorded.

ground_truth.task: extract signal from a multi-gigabyte log without exhausting the host

possible_mistakes: Load the whole log into memory and OOM the host.
Edit/rotate the log during analysis, destroying evidence.
hints: Stream with grep/awk/sed; avoid tools that buffer the whole file.
reference_solution: Extract signal without altering the source
alternative_solution: Copy a bounded slice to scratch and analyze that, leaving the original intact.
edge_cases: Multiline stack traces need a windowed, not line-at-a-time, filter.
